title: Workload-profiled batching autotune and safe apply controller
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Build a batching recommendation engine that profiles per-route and per-customer workload characteristics, generates continuous batching parameter proposals (max_batch_tokens, max_batch_requests, latency_target_ms), and applies them safely via a canary/ramp controller with automatic rollback triggers. The engine should integrate with Redwood Console for visibility, emit explainability metadata for each recommendation, and provide a simulation playground to quantify cost vs latency trade-offs before apply.
proposed_solution: 1) Lightweight profiler running as a sidecar to the serving runtime that collects sequence length distributions, inter-arrival times, KV cache hit/warmth, and token-per-request histograms. 2) Offline heuristics pipeline that turns profiles into candidate parameter sets using rules (percentile-based max_batch, latency headroom margin, cache-awareness). 3) A continuous controller that simulates expected throughput/cost using a fast estimator, proposes a safe canary rollout (1% traffic -> 10% -> 50%), monitors key SLOs (p95 latency, error rate, token cost delta) and auto-rolls back if thresholds exceeded. 4) Integrations: Redwood Console UI, config store API, audit log entries, and a manual approval pathway for high-impact customers.
acceptance_criteria: Profiler collects per-route histograms with <5% sampling overhead in production (measured on staging).
Heuristics generate candidate parameter sets and the offline simulator predicts cost change within +/-10% of observed after controlled experiments.
Controller implements staged canary (1% -> 10% -> 50%) with automated rollback on SLO breach (p95 latency +15% over baseline OR error_rate increase >0.5% OR token-cost increase >8%).
End-to-end e2e tests and integration tests covering apply and rollback flows merged into CI.
Console surfaces per-recommendation expected cost delta, confidence score, and provenance link to profile snapshot.
Runbook documented and on-call notified integration completed for automatic rollback events.
comments: 2026-02-11 Sofia Martinez: Initial spec written and shared in /confluence/Optimize/Batching-Autotune. See doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPT/Batching+Autotune+Spec
2026-02-18 Liam O'Connor: Narrowed profiler to three signals to reduce overhead: seq_len_hist, interarrival_ms, kv_cache_warmth. PoC agent implemented (branch: feat/batch-profiling).

2026-02-25 Engineering review: Reviewed heuristics table. PM asked to add explicit rule for low-traffic routes (do not increase batch size for <10 rps unless >80% seq_len variance). Action: add safe-guards for microservices routes.

2026-03-03 QA: Simulator vs. canary results from internal alpha (customer-mock workload) show 18% cost reduction with p95 latency increase of 3ms (well within SLO). Uploaded experiment notebooks: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/u/1/folders/alpha-batch-sims

2026-03-07 Security: Confirmed no sensitive payloads are stored in profiler snapshots. We will encrypt snapshots at rest and add an ACL in config-store. Security ticket: https://github.com/redwood/security/issues/78
2026-03-10 PM (Aisha Kumar): Request to expose a manual override in Console and require approval for any recommendation with expected customer cost delta >20% or risk score high.

2026-03-12 Liam O'Connor: Implemented canary controller and basic rollback hooks. Integration test failing intermittently on simulated cold-start KV cache scenarios; investigating. PR: https://github.com/redwood/runtime-batcher/pull/4567
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): deploy profiler sidecar to staging clusters, collect 2 weeks of profiles. Phase 2 (internal alpha): run heuristics + simulator on staging profiles and execute controlled canaries against internal dev customers (1 node). Phase 3 (beta): enable recommendations for low-risk routes across non-critical customers with 1% canary. Phase 4 (ga): expose to all customers with manual approval gating for high-impact changes. Each canary step has automated metrics validation and 30-minute monitoring window before ramp.
rollback_criteria: Rollback triggers: p95 latency > baseline * 1.15 for two consecutive measurement windows OR error_rate increase >0.5% absolute OR token-cost increase >8% over baseline after canary start. Rollback steps: immediate traffic re-route to previous config, create incident with auto-populated diagnostic bundle, notify on-call and PM, and annotate recommendation with failure reason.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: heavier profiling increases signal quality but risks CPU overhead; we default to 1% sampling and adaptive ramp-up for suspect routes.
Decision: store 7-day rolling window of profiles per-route and purge older snapshots; keep raw payloads out of snapshots.
Follow-up: Add per-customer opt-out flag and a forensic mode for post-rollback root cause analysis.
Related tickets: ENG-24109 (dynamic batch configurator) is the parent; ensure controller writes configs into the same config-store format.
